title: Automated VPC data-plane upgrade harness integrating Terraform bridge and health-gated rollback
creator: Aisha R. Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a resilient upgrade harness for Private (VPC) data-plane/runtime rollouts that bridges Terraform state transitions with our runtime orchestrator, driven by health-gated canary progression and automated rollback. The harness should: automate Terraform plan/apply sequences safely across tenant slices, verify runtime priming and KV cache health, progressively shift traffic with synthetic and user traffic probes, and support fast, deterministic rollback paths that restore both runtime and infra state (or provide compensating actions) without data loss or significant customer-visible disruption.

Motivation:
Previous private upgrades surfaced two recurring classes of failures: (1) infra-state drift during multi-stage terraform operations (state locking/partial apply) and (2) runtime regressions that only appeared after traffic shift due to unprimed KV caches or kernel-level scheduling differences. Manual interventions caused extended degradation and inconsistent rollback outcomes. This ticket consolidates the Terraform/IaC sequencing with automated runtime health checks and formal rollback playbooks to achieve near-zero-downtime upgrades for customers on VPC/private deployments.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end automation that performs a plan -> staged apply -> verification -> traffic shift -> finalize flow for a tenant slice using our Terraform modules and runtime operators.
- Safe handling of Terraform state: explicit lock and checkpoint before any disruptive change; automatic rollback of Terraform changes if runtime verification fails.
- Health gating: progress only when synthetic probe success % and runtime metrics (99th latency, error rate, kv miss rate) meet thresholds.
- Canary schedule: configurable staged percentages (example default: 1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) with time windows and automatic rollback on regression.
- Rollback determinism: produce the same observable state post-rollback as pre-upgrade (or documented divergence with compensating mitigation).
- Operator visibility: Console runbook step logs, per-tenant timeline, and Grafana dashboard for rollout-specific metrics.

Design highlights:
1) Terraform bridge layer ("tf-bridge"): a small orchestration shim that sequences terraform actions inside a transaction-like flow. Steps: `lock state` -> `create resources in new safe cage (shadow instances)` -> `export plan artifacts` -> `checkpoint state snapshot` -> `mark for traffic shift`. The tf-bridge stores checkpoints in the customer's S3-backed state bucket with immutable tags for recoverability (e.g., s3://redwood-states/<tenant>/checkpoints/<uuid>).

2) Health-driven canary controller: integrates with the runtime orchestrator to apply staged traffic shifts. Uses two probe types:
  - Synthetic probes (internal): deterministic prompts that validate output shape, latency, and token-stability.
  - Production sampling (telemetry): tail-sampled real requests evaluated for error rate and output regression metrics.
Thresholds are configurable per-tenant and per-release; default thresholds: 99th p90 latency not > 10% over baseline, error rate < 0.5%, kv cache warmness > 80%.

3) Rollback strategy: two-tiered rollback paths depending on failure mode:
  - Fast rollback (runtime-only): immediate traffic shift back to previous model/variant + runtime hot-swap; used when telemetry shows behavioral regressions but infra remains healthy. This path is sub-30s to trigger and aims to restore request routing to pre-rollout runtime pool.
  - Full infra rollback: revert Terraform checkpoint and re-provision using the saved checkpoint if the apply caused infra-level failures (e.g., node misconfig, network ACL regressions). This path performs a rollback apply using the tf-bridge checkpoint, then executes a post-rollback reconciliation to ensure running runtime versions match expected.
Compensating actions such as cache priming for the restored pool are part of the runbook.

4) Safe-apply semantics and mid-apply interrupt handling: Recognizing partial terraform apply is the main risk, tf-bridge will: (a) run each tenant in isolated workspace, (b) perform resource creation in a way that is additive (create shadow resources first, switch routing after validation), and (c) if an apply fails mid-step, run an automatic plan-and-revert using the last checkpointed state.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full transactional infra changes would require locking all tenant slices and increase outage risk; instead we chose slice-scoped checkpoints to allow progressive upgrades.
- Aggressive caching/priming reduces customer-visible regressions but increases cost during rollout; we set priming as configurable per-tenant and added a cost/benefit flag in the rollout config.
- Strictly automated infra rollback can be surprising for customers; we will surface human-confirmation options for high-impact rollouts (P0 customers or large clusters).

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Build tf-bridge microservice and Terraform module updates (2 sprints): workspace checkpointing, S3 checkpoint storage, shadow resource pattern.
2) Extend runtime orchestrator controller (1 sprint): health-gated canary controller that consumes tf-bridge events and controls traffic-shift steps.
3) Probe library and default probe manifests (0.5 sprint): synthetic prompts and telemetry evaluation hooks.
4) Runbook + Console integration (0.5 sprint): per-rollout timeline, manual abort button, rollback artifact links, and dashboard panels.
5) Internal dogfood: apply to internal staging tenants, then invited customers.

Operational runbook (high level):
- Preflight: run `tf-bridge preflight <tenant>` to create checkpoint; run `priming` job if enabled; verify baseline metrics.
- Start: kick off `rollout start --plan-id <uuid>`; watch canary progression and synthetic probe logs.
- Failure case (fast): can trigger `rollout abort` to immediate traffic fallback; system will record a causal timeline and mark the release as failed.
- Failure case (infra): system will stop progression and attempt `tf-bridge revert --checkpoint <uuid>`; notify on-call and run reconciliation jobs.

- Prototype tf-bridge code (internal repo): https://git.internal.redwood/infra/tf-bridge/pulls/27
- Terraform module changes: https://git.internal.redwood/terraform-modules/vpc-upgrade-bridge/commits
- Runtime canary controller PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4219
- Dashboard (staging): https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/rollouts/upgrade-harness

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should we require human approval for infra-level rollbacks for tenants with >X nodes? (proposal: X=50; seeking PM/SA input.)
- Do we add auto-priming as a default for all customers or opt-in? (cost vs stability tradeoff)
- How to represent rollback audit trail for compliance customers (we need immutable artifacts tied to SAML identity).

Acceptance testing plan:
- Unit + e2e tests for tf-bridge checkpoint/restore flows.
- Chaos test: simulate partial apply and verify system runs revert to checkpoint without customer-facing downtime.
- Load test: run staged canary with real traffic profile (internal stress tenant) and verify thresholds trigger expected behavior.
- Dry-run: produce rollout timeline and logs without shifting production traffic.

Notes from architecture review (2025-02-25):
- Security flagged the S3 checkpointing flow: we must encrypt checkpoints with customer KMS and ensure IAM policies prevent cross-tenant access. (Action: infra-security to provide KMS design.)
- Network team requested explicit ACL rollback tests.

Known non-goals for this ticket:
- Handling of schema-changing model updates (that require data migration) — those will be handled by separate migration tooling.
- Multi-tenant shared-hosting upgrades are out-of-scope for this first phase.
